summary.heading: Current state
summary.text: The SNB left the policy rate unchanged at 0% on 24 September 2026 (V). The current policy rate remains 0.00%, valid from 20 June 2025 (V). The staff baseline for the 10 December 2026 assessment is a hold at 0%, with a higher short-term conditional inflation forecast and a live discussion of whether 0% remains appropriate. Hawk/dove score: +1 (slightly hawkish tilt into December; committee barometer scale −5 to +5; Einschätzung, keine Formel). Incoming data since the meeting have moved against the September Q4 forecast of 0.7%: headline CPI was 0.8% y/y in August at the time of the decision and has since printed 1.0% in September and 1.5% in October (V: BFS, 3 November 2026). Core 1 remains 0.5% in October, unchanged from September (V: BFS). The rise is imported and energy-driven (imported goods +3.7%, petroleum products +40.3% y/y in October; V: BFS). A 1.5% October print makes a Q4 average of 0.7% highly unlikely without a sharp reversal in November–December (d). Official monthly EUR/CHF and USD/CHF (SNB cube devkum, to October 2026) show a June–September depreciation and a partial October retracement against the euro, with the franc still weaker against the dollar than in early summer (V / (d)). Staff view, not the Governing Board’s and not official SNB staff work. A staff LIK component nowcast is not yet available.

nowcast_hint: There is no staff LIK component nowcast on this page; that model is pending. Official BFS, SECO and SNB readings are shown with their V / (d) labels. The 10 December policy call and the hawk/dove score are staff judgment.
nowcast_note: The 10 December baseline (hold at 0%) and the hawk/dove score of +1 are staff judgment (Einschätzung, keine Formel), not a formula and not a market-implied probability. A staff LIK nowcast point for November 2026 is not published: the component model is pending, and an unsealed research prototype is not shown. Quarterly headline y/y figures of 0.17% (Q1), 0.56% (Q2) and 0.72% (Q3) are derived (d) from average official monthly BFS indices; the SNB’s September “observed” table printed 0.2 and 0.6 for Q1 and Q2 (consistent after rounding) and left Q3–Q4 blank.

nowcasts.source: Staff judgment, SNB baseline note, 12 November 2026
nowcasts.rationale: Central staff call: hold at 0%, with a higher short-term inflation forecast and a live discussion of whether 0% remains appropriate. A hike is not the baseline while core remains at 0.5% and the SNB continues to look through energy, but the October print has made a purely mechanical “forecast still in the band, therefore hold and say little” meeting less comfortable.

nowcasts.source: Staff judgment, SNB baseline note, 12 November 2026
nowcasts.rationale: Einschätzung, keine Formel. Slightly hawkish tilt: last action a hold at 0% with an expansionary self-assessment, but “increased” FX-intervention willingness withdrawn after franc depreciation, and two subsequent CPI prints (1.0%, then 1.5%) sit well above the September Q4 forecast of 0.7%. Core 0.5% and the look-through-energy reaction function keep a December hike out of the baseline and cap the score at +1 rather than +2 or higher.

recent_data.release: SNB summary of the September Governing Board discussion

staff_hint: Staff view, not the Governing Board and not official SNB staff work. The hawk/dove score is judgment, not a formula. Market-implied SNB pricing was not obtained.

staff_view.lead: Baseline for 10 December: hold at 0%, with a higher inflation forecast and a live discussion of whether 0% remains appropriate. Hawk/dove score: +1 (slightly hawkish tilt; scale −5 to +5; Einschätzung, keine Formel).
bullets: Last action, 24 September: policy rate held at 0% (valid from 20 June 2025). The September conditional forecast, assuming 0% over the entire horizon, stayed inside 0–2% and put annual inflation at 0.7% in 2026 and 0.8% in 2027 and 2028 (V).

Incoming CPI has moved against that Q4 path: 1.0% in September and 1.5% in October, after 0.8% in August at the time of the decision (V: BFS). Core 1 is still 0.5%. The rise is imported and energy-driven (imported +3.7%, petroleum products +40.3%; V). A 1.5% October print makes a Q4 average of 0.7% highly unlikely without a sharp November–December reversal (d).

The September discussion (published 22 October) remains the best official read of the reaction function: conditions had eased because franc depreciation outweighed a slight rise in rates; policy is expansionary; expectations well anchored; no second-round effects; “increased willingness to intervene is no longer necessary,” while standard FX willingness was retained. No explicit guidance on a return to a negative policy rate (V).
Activity: SECO Q2 sport-event-adjusted GDP +1.5% q/q (V); Q3 not yet published (provisional date 30 November). Official SNB growth forecast 1.5–2% in 2026 and around 1.5% in 2027 (V).

Official monthly FX (devkum, to October): June–September depreciation and a partial October retracement against the euro; the franc still weaker against the dollar than in early summer (V / (d)). Sight deposits 452.9 bn on 6 November, about CHF 15.6 bn below the June assessment week (V / (d)) — evidence, not proof, of FX intervention.

A staff LIK component nowcast is not yet available and is not shown. Market-implied SNB path (SARON OIS, futures, hike probabilities): not obtained from any free official source; not estimated. Hard gap.
staff_view.policy: Baseline — hold at 0% (~central): the Board revises the short-term conditional forecast up, keeps it inside 0–2% at a constant 0% rate or close to it, repeats the standard FX-willingness sentence without restoring “increased willingness,” and stresses energy, the Middle East, and the absence (or otherwise) of second-round effects. Hawkish — hike 25 bp, or a hold with a clearly tighter bias / a forecast that no longer sits comfortably at a constant 0% — would need November (and any early-December) CPI that keeps headline elevated and lifts core or domestic inflation, or evidence of second-round effects, or a further material franc depreciation; a first hike since the 2025 easing would be a regime shift from “look through energy.” Dovish — cut, or a return to “increased” FX-intervention willingness — is the less likely tail on the current information set. A return to a negative policy rate is not signalled in any official text fetched for the note. The already-negative above-threshold sight-deposit rate (−0.25%) is a feature of the tiered remuneration system, not a policy-rate signal (V).

taylor.title: Taylor-type comparison (d) — illustrative, not an SNB rule
taylor.note: Specification (Taylor 1993 form): iT = r* + inflation + 0.5 × (inflation − 1%) + 0.5 × output gap. π* = 1% is the mid-point of the SNB’s 0–2% range (V for the range, (d) for the mid-point). r* is not observed and is illustrated at 0%, not as an estimate of Swiss equilibrium. No official output-gap series was fetched; y is illustrated at 0 and −0.5 pp as stylised “mild slack,” consistent only qualitatively with the SNB’s September remark that capacity utilisation was below average, especially in manufacturing. Not a fitted SNB reaction function.

caveats: Report date 12 November 2026, Europe/Zurich; no time of day was recorded on the baseline note. Official sources were fetched on 12 November 2026. Labels: V = verified from a primary official source with date stated; U = unverified; (d) = derived by the desk; own estimate / Einschätzung, keine Formel = staff judgment. This page does not generate or refresh figures.

The 10 December baseline (hold at 0%) and the hawk/dove score of +1 are staff judgment, not a formula, not a market-implied probability, and not official SNB guidance. The September assessment contained no explicit guidance on a return to a negative policy rate.

A staff LIK component nowcast is not yet available and is not shown. The LIK month-on-month chart is a benchmark backtest only (seasonal mean, seasonal naïve, and related simple rules). An unsealed research prototype is omitted from this public page.

The September 2026 conditional forecast quarterly path was read from the official press-release PDF table image, aligned to the printed year-separator gridlines, not from a machine-readable SNB file. Annual averages 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.8 also appear in the body text (V). Quarterly headline y/y of 0.17 / 0.56 / 0.72 for 2026 Q1–Q3 is derived (d) from average official monthly indices.
SARON on this page is the SNB’s two-decimal republication of SIX. The legally authoritative six-decimal SIX fixing was not fetched. The latest such SNB print is 10 November 2026, not 11 November.

The Taylor-type comparison is illustrative and assumption-dependent (d): r* is not observed, no official output-gap series was fetched, and the specification is not a fitted SNB rule. The SNB’s revealed reaction function, as written down in September, is closer to a core / look-through-energy / conditional-forecast reading than to a headline Taylor.

Sight-deposit and FX-reserve stock moves are not intervention figures. Published quarterly FX-intervention (purchase/sale) figures for 2026 Q2 or Q3 were not located in the cubes queried for the note or in the text of Quarterly Bulletin 3/2026.

The end-October SNB balance sheet is not yet published (latest official month is September, published 30 October). Sight deposits after 6 November are not in the cube published on 9 November. No later official trade-weighted CHF index was fetched after the SNB’s own “around 3%” TWI depreciation figure as at the September assessment.

November 2026 CPI had not been published at the time of the note; it is due on 2 December 2026, 08:30 (official BFS calendar, V, recorded in later desk feasibility notes). SECO Q3 GDP is not yet published (provisional official date 30 November 2026, 09:00). Q2 y/y was not extracted from the SECO tables (q/q is the official headline used here). The June 2026 SNB growth figure that was later raised was not re-fetched.
